look_here_first: Look at the flowering stem: many short oat-like racemes project and droop from mostly one side of the central axis.
project_tracker_diagnostic: Warm-season bunchgrass with numerous short racemes arranged mostly along one side of the inflorescence axis; flowering spikelets often show conspicuous reddish to orange anthers.

project_inclusion.range_basis: BONAP Texas county distribution supported by explicit Central Texas/target-zone county records; no county presence inferred.

morphology_keys.habit: Perennial warm-season bunchgrass; culms erect to ascending from a tufted base.
morphology_keys.leaves: Mostly basal to lower-culm blades, narrow and flat to folded; margins and surfaces can feel rough.
morphology_keys.inflorescence: An elongated central axis bearing many short lateral racemes; the racemes characteristically hang or project from mostly one side.
morphology_keys.spikelets: Several spikelets are packed along each short raceme; racemes detach as units when mature.
morphology_keys.floral_detail: Reddish to orange anthers are often conspicuous during flowering.
best_field_traits: racemes concentrated mostly on one side of the central axis

comparisons.key_distinctions: Start with inflorescence architecture. Sideoats grama usually carries many more short racemes distributed down an elongated axis, creating the unmistakable one-sided 'oats hanging off a stem' look.

ecological_notes.habitat: Prairies, open grasslands, roadsides, rocky calcareous sites, and managed native plantings across Central Texas.
ecological_notes.learning_note: A high-value first Bouteloua because the inflorescence architecture can often be recognized at walking distance.
